meta.comment: Central content for the AR scientific poster. All physical values are the REAL parameters of the buoyant-jet test case (laminar, Re~100) and its wall-heat-loss study — not generic placeholders. Edit freely; the app reloads from this file.

title: Data-based Numerical Simulation of Buoyant Jet Flow
subtitle: Master's Thesis · recurrence-CFD of a laminar buoyant jet — adiabatic baseline & wall heat loss
author: Mochamad Bukhori Zainun (k12438440)
institution: Department of Particulate Flow Modelling, JKU Linz
abstract: A short CFD run records the recurring flow patterns of a laminar buoyant jet in a closed water tank. Recurrence-CFD (rCFD) then replays those patterns to transport the temperature field at a fraction of the cost, with a face-swap diffusion operator (parameter f_sd) restoring the missing mixing. Switching on wall heat loss then stress-tests the idea: at the reference case h = 100, replaying the reused adiabatic database recovers only about a third of the true cooling, quantifying where the reuse assumption breaks.

groups.heading: Key findings
items: rCFD reproduces the 600 s buoyant-jet temperature transport from one short CFD run, ~263× faster.
Adiabatic: best mixing strength is metric-dependent — f_sd = 0.000 for mean temperature, f_sd = 0.500 for the thermal centre of gravity (CoG RMSE 0.069 mm).
Wall heat loss: at the reference case h = 100, replaying the reused adiabatic database recovers only about a third of the true cooling (rCFD 3.03 K vs CFD 9.79 K).

groups.heading: Physical interpretation
items: A warm laminar jet (Re ≈ 100) rises by buoyancy and builds a stable warm layer under the ceiling.
Two counter-rotating vortices form from entrainment; buoyancy tilts them upward.
Mixing beyond what the shift map carries is supplied by the face-swap operator.

groups.heading: Wall heat loss — a stress test
items: A top-surface sink q = h(T−T∞) is added as a balance-registered source term; the physical value is gentle (h ≈ 8 W/m²K), so a stronger h = 100 is used as the reference case to make the cooling visible.
At h = 100 the full CFD cools by 9.79 K; the frozen adiabatic replay cools only 3.03 K — it misses the buoyancy-driven overturning that keeps fresh warm fluid at the cooled surface.
The shortfall is advective, motivating a non-adiabatic (or multi-regime) database rather than reusing the adiabatic one.

groups.heading: Numerical stability
items: Structured 1 mm cubic cells (~85,625) keep the C2C shift maps exact.
Face-swap diffusion is mass- and energy-conservative; above the 1/8 cap it splits into inner sweeps.
Laminar solver matches the regime, avoiding spurious turbulent mixing.
